items.title: ArtCraft: Ten Open-Source Creative Apps in One LinuxServer Docker Container
items.summary: I am always interested in finding new open-source software, especially when it offers free alternatives to programs that usually cost money. ArtCraft is a project I recently came across that has quite a few creative apps for photo editing, graphic design, video editing and more. LinuxServer.io has put ten of these apps into a single Docker container. You get a full Linux desktop that you can access from your web browser, with all ten apps ready to use. If you already have a home server running Docker, this is a nice way to try some new software without having to install each program on your computer.

items.title: QRdx is an Open-Source QR Code Generator You Can Self-Host
items.summary: QR codes are everywhere, but finding a generator that offers decent customization without watermarks, mandatory accounts, or subscriptions can be surprisingly frustrating. Most tools handle basic URLs just fine, but things get complicated when you want custom designs, editable destinations, or a little more control over how your codes are managed. QRdx is an open-source QR code platform that brings these capabilities together in a single application. It offers a browser-based editor for creating customized QR codes, along with dynamic links, scan analytics, hosted landing pages, and several developer tools.

items.title: Debian 13.8 Released with 150 Security Updates and 122 Bug Fixes
items.summary: The Debian Project has announced the release of Debian 13.8, the eighth maintenance update to its stable Debian 13 “Trixie” series. items.title: On this day in space! Nov. 21, 1676: Danish astronomer discovers speed of light — by accident — while observing Jupiter's moon Io
items.summary: On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of light. Before Rømer figured it out, scientists thought that light travels instantaneously, or infinitely fast. Rømer disproved this almost by accident when he was studying Jupiter's moon Io. He was trying to figure out how long it takes Io to orbit Jupiter in hopes of using it as a cosmic clock. He watched Io disappear behind Jupiter and reappear on the other side. He did this over and over every 42 hours for years. To his surprise, the timing of the eclipses was not consistent.

items.summary: Humans experience and interact with the world through sensory information. This could mean learning correspondences between the sound of bird chirps and the word “robin,” or being able to visually identify and follow your friend “Sarah” in a crowd of people. In many cases, people are able to draw on their latent “multimodal” knowledge — information across multiple data types, from audio to video to text or spoken word — to perform these tasks without many, or sometimes even any, examples. Multimodal foundation models of artificial intelligence are increasingly gaining capabilities that mimic this.

items.title: NASA’s Curiosity Mars Rover Collects Samples
items.summary: This Nov. 16 collage shows 49 drill holes captured by NASA’s Curiosity Mars rover as of November 2026. Each hole represents a sample collected from rocks on the Martian surface; Curiosity’s drill, located on the end of its robotic arm, drops pulverized rock samples into instruments in its belly that analyze their composition. Learn more about Curiosity.

items.title: Dry weather pattern holds across Arizona
items.summary: Light winds and dry skies will dominate Arizona heading into Thanksgiving week, with Phoenix highs in the low 70s before a warmer, dry weekend following the holiday.

items.title: New approach enables physically consistent AI models of chaotic systems
items.summary: Modeling of complex, chaotic processes such as weather and climate patterns and turbulent flows in aviation or in ocean currents has advanced enormously in recent years. However, such models are still prone to drift into physically impossible predictions over time. Now, researchers with MIT’s Laboratory for Information and Decision Systems (LIDS) have found a way to introduce physics-based restrictions on machine learning models that can ensure that such models never exceed realistic bounds, based on what is actually possible in the real world.

items.title: AI may not work like the human brain after all, scientists discover
items.summary: AI may not think like the human brain after all, according to a striking new discovery that challenges how scientists understand artificial intelligence. Researchers found that even AI models that closely predict brain activity may rely on internal processes the brain doesn't use, raising important questions about their reliability in neuroscience research.

items.title: How Medieval Writers Responded to the Peasants’ Revolt
items.summary: The Peasants’ Revolt of 1381 shook medieval England, but how did the people who lived through it respond in writing? From messages circulated among the rebels to the works of John Gower and Geoffrey Chaucer, the uprising left its mark on medieval literature. In this excerpt from Chaucer’s England, published by Yale University Press, Nicholas Orme examines how the revolt was represented by those who supported it, feared it, or looked back upon it years later. The rising spread not only through word of mouth but in writing: a further sign of literacy among some of the lower orders.

items.title: SpaceX will retire 1st Starship upper stage ever caught by 'chopsticks,' Elon Musk says
items.summary: The first Starship upper stage that SpaceX ever successfully recovered won't fly again. That vehicle, known as Ship 42, launched Nov. 13 on Starship 's 15th test flight. A day later, it returned from orbit, nestling softly into the "chopstick" arms of its launch tower at SpaceX 's Starbase site in South Texas. Ship 42 made it through Flight 15 in good condition, according to SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk, who said it "could probably be reflown with a few weeks of refurbishment." But that's not going to happen.

items.title: Aviation Coalition Presses Congress on ATC Funding
items.summary: The Modern Skies Coalition launched a national advertising campaign Friday urging Congress to provide additional funding for air traffic control modernization. The campaign, called “ACT NOW,” includes a 30-second video scheduled to appear on television networks, streaming services and social media platforms. The coalition represents more than 50 aviation organizations, including airlines, general aviation groups, airports and labor unions. The campaign follows the Nov. 13 nationwide ground stop, which lasted nearly five hours after telecommunications problems disrupted air traffic control operations.

items.title: SpaceX lenders don’t want Elon Musk launching their collateral into space
items.summary: Lenders backing SpaceX’s latest $43 billion debt package, which is secured by its advanced AI chips, have tried to bar Elon Musk from firing the collateral into space as part of his plan for orbital data centers. The world’s richest man has outlined ambitious plans to power AI models with data centers cooled by the vacuum of space. That will require packing satellites full of advanced chips. SpaceX has said it plans to use the chips involved in the debt deal on Earth.

items.title: Here are 7 great reasons rural drivers SHOULD embrace EVs in 2027
items.summary: America’s heartland is full of rural communities that are miles away from its major cities, both geographically and culturally – but that doesn’t mean these more sparsely populated regions can’t reap the benefits of electrification. In fact, EVs offer rural drivers even more benefits than they do to city-dwellers! more…

items.title: Stream It Or Skip It: ‘Percy Jackson And The Olympians’ Season 3 on Disney+, where Percy & pals have to stop a war
items.summary: The series based on Rick Riordan's popular fantasy novels seems to take a darker turn in Season 3.

items.title: A game you cannot win unless you have a quantum computer
items.summary: On a superconducting processor, we turned one of quantum mechanics’ strangest features into something you can measure, benchmark, and put to work across systems as large as 105 qubits. Here is a Sunday paper-style puzzle you can try right now. Draw a 3×3 grid. Fill every cell with either +1 or −1, subject to two rules: each row must multiply to +1, and each column must multiply to −1. You didn’t manage it, right? There is an elegant reason for that. For a row to multiply to +1, it needs an even number of −1s.

items.title: Russia-bound ship still on fire after attack in Gulf of Finland
items.summary: Rescue and firefighting efforts are continuing for a Russian cargo vessel hit by a drone attack in the eastern Gulf of Finland, authorities have said. The ship - the Sparta II - was bound for Russia's Baltic exclave Kaliningrad when it was hit on Saturday morning, before drifting into Finnish waters. Finnish defence forces said Ukraine was likely behind the attack. Kyiv has yet to comment. Finland's Border Guard said on Sunday that work was ongoing to make sure the cargo ship did not sink but it was not aware of any danger to surrounding maritime traffic.

items.title: Anthropic worker claims to have solved a holy grail of math problems with the help of AI
items.summary: A mathematician who works for artificial intelligence giant Anthropic claims he has solved a holy grail of math problems with the help of the company's AI tool Claude.

items.title: Horror Series ‘FROM’ Is a Massive Hit on Netflix With 5 Billion Minutes Viewed Across Three Weeks
items.summary: It was one month ago that the MGM+ horror series “FROM” hopped over to Netflix, with the first three seasons of the four season series (a fifth and final season is on the way!) now streaming on Netflix. And the show’s arrival on Netflix has introduced the hit horror series to a whole new audience, with Deadline reporting on just how massive that new audience has been. Deadline details, “MGM+ horror series FROM raked in 1.69 billion minutes viewed from November 2 to 8, easily putting it atop Nielsen’s streaming charts for the week.

items.title: Tesla FSD V15 Makes Your Drive Look Like Grand Theft Auto
items.summary: FSD V15’s GTA-style follow camera shows where your Tesla plans to turn or park. Tesla claims a 25-fold drop in critical driver interventions but doesn't share the baseline reference. V15 learns from other Tesla drivers’ routes at the start and end of trips. Tesla says it also spots potholes and debris more reliably. Tesla’s latest version of Full Self-Driving lets you swing a virtual camera around your car like you’re cruising through Leonida in Grand Theft Auto. It’s a neat trick, especially when you consider that the Tesla has to generate the scenery as it goes.

items.title: DietPi 10.9 Released with Support for Five New Single-Board Computers
items.summary: DietPi, the lightweight Debian-based Linux distribution optimized for single-board computers and server applications, has released version 10.9, introducing images for several new single-board computers. These include the Odroid C5 with Amlogic’s S905X5M processor and the Orange Pi 6 and 6 Plus, both featuring the 12-core CIX P1 SoC. Support has also been added for the Orange Pi Zero 4, featuring the Allwinner A733 processor and Gigabit Ethernet, and the Orange Pi 4A with the Allwinner T527. However, the latter currently has a kernel limitation that prevents proper CPU scheduling, leaving its cores running at a fixed 768 MHz.

items.title: Tesla launches FSD v15, targets its biggest weaknesses, from signs to potholes
items.summary: Tesla has started rolling out “Full Self-Driving” v15, and its list of improvements reads like a list of FSD’s biggest current weaknesses: sign detection, potholes, and speed handling in school zones. Tesla also claims “25x better handling of safety critical cases” and is adding a new live visualization that looks seriously impressive. If the driving improvements are as real as the visuals, this is a big update. more…

items.title: How much does charging an EV really cost? This Redditor says $7 per month
items.summary: One of the most common questions asked by first-time EV buyers is about the cost of electricity. Whether they plan to charge at home or find charging in the wild, everyone wants to know what to expect when it comes time to top off their batteries. One EV owner did the math after two months of EV ownership and came up with a surprising number: $7 a month. more…

items.title: Pentagon UAP files part 8: Radar track analysis and more
items.summary: The U.S. Pentagon released the 8th batch of its UAP files on November 20, 2026. This Pentagon UAP files release contains 43 new files altogether. Among these, 40 are documents and three are videos. The release is part of a continuing rollout of formerly classified files, every few weeks. So far, there’s still been no “smoking gun” to show that alien craft are visiting Earth. But the files are interesting! The 2027 lunar calendar from EarthSky is now available! See the moon’s phase for every day of the year.

items.title: Evan Edward designs "seductive" Miami Beach pied-à-terre
items.summary: Miami 's nightlife scene in the 1990s informed the saturated colours and metallic accents used by local studio Evan Edward inside this apartment in the oceanside city, illustrating what the studio calls its "high-impact minimalism" approach. Designed for an international family with "personal ties to the city's storied nightlife era", the Miami Beach pied-à-terre reflects the hedonistic era that left a distinct stylistic impression. items.title: Tesla Cybertruck’s already impressive turning radius gets even tighter
items.summary: Tesla is rolling out an update that makes the Cybertruck turn even tighter, improving on what was already one of the best turning radiuses you can get in a full-size pickup. But there’s a catch. It only works on 2027 model year Cybertrucks, and Tesla plans to stop building the truck by the end of next summer. more…

items.summary: On Nov. 14, 2026, SpaceX made spaceflight history as teams brought Ship 42 back from space to be caught by Pad 2’s tower. Launch and Booster 22 Splashdown Following a smooth countdown, with the license received about four hours before launch, Booster 22 and Ship 42 lifted off on Nov. 13 at 4:47:36 pm CST (22:47:36 UTC).

items.title: Delta Flight Stops Taxiing After Cat Escapes Carrier and Runs Loose in Cabin
items.summary: BOSTON – A Delta Air Lines (DL) flight bound for Tampa was forced to stop taxiing at Boston (BOS) Logan International Airport on Friday morning after a passenger’s cat escaped its kennel and began roaming the aircraft cabin. The incident occurred shortly before 7:00 AM, as Flight 2706 prepared to depart for Tampa International Airport (TPA). The unexpected situation prompted the flight crew to request a brief hold from air traffic control while they dealt with the loose animal. The aircraft remained on the taxiway until the cat was secured, resulting in an approximately 15-minute departure delay, although the flight ultimately arrived in Tampa on schedule.

items.title: detour 2026 proves ‘better, not perfect’ is all it takes across 14 installations and a pop-up shop
items.summary: 14 EXPERIMENTS AND ONE POP-UP TAKE OVER DETOUR 2026 From November 20 to 29, 2026, Hong Kong’s signature design festival deTour returns to PMQ under the guiding curatorial theme ‘BETTER, NOT PERFECT: Prototypes for Tomorrow’. Across PMQ’s Courtyard and Marketplace, 14 commissioned installations and experiments from Hong Kong, Chinese Mainland, and international studios explore speculative urban concepts, material transformations, and the Asia debut of US inventor Matty Benedetto of Unnecessary Inventions.

items.title: Claude Code Has Been Leaking Secrets Through Its "Don't Ask Again" Feature

items.title: Top Wall Street analysts favor these 3 dividend stocks for strong returns
items.summary: Investors often favor dividend stocks for their regular income and the promise of potential share price appreciation. items.title: SpaceX launches classified mission for US Space Force from California (video)
items.summary: SpaceX launched a classified mission for the U.S. Space Force tonight (Nov. 20), sending a mystery payload to orbit from California's central coast. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base tonight at 11:20 p.m. EST (8:20 p.m. local California time; 0420 GMT on Nov. 21), on a Space Force mission called USSF-317. The Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth about 8.5 minutes later, touching down in the Pacific Ocean atop the SpaceX drone ship "Of Course I Still Love You." It was the 11th launch and landing for this booster, which is designated B1100.

items.title: The Nasdaq is in freefall. Here's one stock to look at
items.summary: I asked Claude after Friday's close what I should do about the tanking stock market. Its advice was surprisingly useful: avoid panic selling and look for opportunities. A 40 VIX, which it touched Friday, might provide those opportunities. Specifically, a higher VIX (higher options premiums) signals fear, but it also creates an opportunity to sell elevated premium in some premium stocks, like Amazon. Amazon's cloud business is growing at its fastest pace in nearly five years. AWS revenue rose 39.3% YoY in the third quarter, and management reported a $578 billion backlog.

items.title: My 10-year-old laptop runs better on Linux today than it did on Windows the day I bought it
items.summary: It was 2016, and my old Lenovo laptop had become battered and unusable for anything performance-focused. Its discrete AMD GPU wasn't even showing up anymore, and the Intel Core i3 second-generation processor was gasping for breath with new software. So I kept it for basic browsing, downloading, and small software tasks, and had to get a new one with a slightly better configuration. I purchased a new HP laptop with more powerful specs than my old machine, with 4GB DDR4 memory.

items.title: Can teams of AI agents recreate the chain reaction of human decisions?

Australians alone bought 39.7 million rolls from the Woolworths supermarket chain in a single week, according to the store's 2020 annual report. It's not the only time that fear of a shortage spiraled into one.

items.title: How Google Duplex evolved to also call businesses for you in Gemini
items.summary: When we introduced Google Duplex in 2018, it pioneered natural voice conversations between AI and local businesses over the phone. Since then, this technology has worked behind the scenes across many Google products. These capabilities are integrated directly in Tasks in Gemini. Completing tasks like making dinner reservations or booking a hair appointment is time consuming. Live phone conversations move fast and rarely follow a script. The person on the other end can say almost anything, often revising their thoughts mid-sentence – and people often rely on subtle tone changes to indicate whose turn it is to speak.

items.title: Woman dies after being hit by car on I-10 in central Phoenix
items.summary: PHOENIX (AZFamily) — A woman is dead after being hit by a car on Interstate 10 in central Phoenix early Sunday morning. Just after 5 a.m., troopers received reports of a woman walking across eastbound I-10 between 12th and 16th Streets, according to the Arizona Department of Public Safety. Troopers say about two minutes later, the woman was struck and killed by a vehicle. Authorities do not believe the driver was impaired at the time of the crash. Drivers should avoid the area, as eastbound I-10 is expected to remain closed until about 8 a.m., according to DPS.

items.title: Highway partially blocked after crash near Buckeye
items.summary: BUCKEYE, AZ (AZFamily) — Drivers traveling between Gila Bend and Buckeye should plan for delays after a three-vehicle crash on State Route 85. Just before 1 p.m., troopers responded to the crash on Northbound SR 85 at Narramore Road, near the Gila River, according to the Arizona Department of Public Safety. items.title: Belgian strike to disrupt flights at Brussels and Charleroi airports
items.summary: Brussels Airport (BRU) expects major flight disruption on November 23, after some air traffic controllers at Belgian air navigation service provider skeyes announced they would join a national demonstration. The airport said most arriving and departing flights will have to be cancelled because skeyes will not be able to provide normal air traffic control services during the action. The disruption is expected from 7 a.m. to 9 p.m. local time (6 a.m. – 8 p.m. UTC). Skeyes unable to provide normal ATC services According to Skeyes, the expected number of staff would not be enough to safely handle regular air traffic during the strike.

items.title: Babies in ancient Greek colony started solid food at 3 months but nursed for nearly 4 years, chemical signatures suggest
items.summary: Over 2,500 years ago, Himera was a Greek colony inhabited by local Sicilians, Phoenicians and Greeks. Despite their diverse cultural backgrounds, they all shared one thing: they began weaning their babies early and continued for a long time.

items.title: Noninvasive brain interface uses AI suggestions to convey messages nearly three times faster
items.summary: Rutgers engineers have developed one of the fastest noninvasive brain-computer communication interfaces of its kind, leveraging artificial intelligence (AI) to translate brain activity into words and phrases at record-level speeds.

items.title: Possible Ancient Tavern Investigated Near Baghdad
items.summary: BAGHDAD, IRAQ— La Brújula Verde reports that researchers led by Nicola Laneri of the University of Catania are continuing to excavate the site of a 3,800-year-old building at Tell Muhammad, which is located near the Tigris River in central Iraq. A cuneiform tablet recording an agreement to borrow barley and beer was found in one of the building’s rooms. The contract had been signed in front of two witnesses. The space where the tablet was uncovered features a semicircular mudbrick counter facing the street, and a mudbrick basin that may have been used for brewing or making bread.

items.title: KDE Releases Kwi 0.1, Its New GPU-Accelerated Terminal Emulator
items.summary: KDE has released Kwi 0.1, the first official version of its new GPU-accelerated terminal emulator, built with Qt Quick and Kirigami and using Ghostty’s libghostty-vt as a backend. As we reported earlier, Kwi is developed as a modern alternative to Konsole, with GPU-accelerated rendering and integration with the KDE ecosystem. With version 0.1 now available, users can install and test it directly from Flathub. Source archives are also available through KDE’s download servers for distribution maintainers.

items.title: Students Recover Roman Military Artifacts in Northern England
items.summary: REDESDALE, ENGLAND—A student excavation at a site on the Roman frontier in northeastern England uncovered several artifacts linked to Roman elites and military service, according to a statement released by Newcastle University. The first, a piece of gold chain measuring almost three inches long, is made of individual rings that were pinched into figure-eight shapes, folded, and then interwoven. A small lead sheet bearing a Latin inscription may have been used as a personal message, a curse tablet, or a commercial seal.

items.title: One tiny optical sensor uses AI to pinpoint touch and measure movement
items.summary: Picture a keyboard that knows not only which key you pressed, but also how hard you pressed it, using just one tiny sensor. Research from Washington University in St. Louis is paving the way for smaller, smarter sensors that bring this idea closer to reality. The new work has potential applications for robotics, human health monitoring and cybersecurity.

items.title: Well-Preserved Murals Uncovered at Roman Residence in Spain
items.summary: MÉRIDA, SPAIN—According to the Greek Reporter, well-preserved wall paintings have been discovered in a courtyard surrounded by columns within a Roman dwelling at Huerta de Otero, an archaeological site in western Spain, by archaeologists led by José Vargas. The paintings feature images of peacocks, cranes, two deer chased by a feline predator, and mythological figures such as a satyr. A mosaic depicting Medusa was previously discovered in a room of the house. It is not yet known who occupied the house, which covers more than 54,000 square feet. For more on the Medusa mosaic, go to “ The Medusa of Mérida.”

items.title: How to Survive in the Middle Ages: A Medieval Survival Guide
items.summary: Imagine being transported back to medieval England. Could you survive without modern medicine, technology, or even the ability to speak the local language? Life in the Middle Ages would certainly present challenges, but your modern knowledge and skills might give you some surprising advantages. Here’s how you could not only survive in the medieval world, but perhaps even prosper. The popular YouTube channel The Infographics Show has tackled this question in its video Why You Wouldn’t Survive In Medieval Time.

items.title: Homelabber’s second-gen Optane build uses two RTX 3090s to run 2.8-trillion-parameter Kimi AI model at 3.11 tokens per second
items.summary: A homelabber detailed improvements to the second-gen Optane AI build in a follow-up post on Reddit, showing the addition of two RTX 3090s to run the 2.8-trillion-parameter Moonshot Kimi K3 model at 3.11 tokens per second. Transferring almost half the model onto a RAM drive added a significant 41% to generation speed and 26% to prompt evaluation. The extra fans are still needed, though, as the persistent Optane memory gets very hot. That speed is not the most impressive, but it comes with 16.8 tokens per second for prompt evaluation, with 45 of 94 shards, or 414 GB out of 865 GB, living on a RAM drive.

items.title: This scientist proves which problems computers can’t solve quickly
items.summary: Dor Minzer remembers sitting in an undergraduate computation class at Tel Aviv University. He was intrigued by his professor and soon found himself pulled into a new world: the mystifying intersection of math and computation, first laid out by Alan Turing during World War II. Working with the professor, Minzer became deeply interested in the limitations of what computers can and can’t do. “My part is actually to prove not only do I not know how to do it, but I can prove that it’s impossible,” Minzer says.

items.title: How do scientists learn from failure? This researcher has clues
items.summary: Yian Yin seeks to understand the dynamics of science itself. The computational social scientist is particularly interested in how innovations happen and how they may be accelerated. “I want to understand what the secret sources or recipes of success are,” says Yin, of Cornell University. He applied machine learning techniques to accepted and rejected research proposals to understand how scientists learn from failures. What he found was that scientists fail, and they fail often. Some switched gears after some rejections, but others who continued their research and incorporated feedback found success at a faster rate.

items.title: How do tumors talk to nerves? This scientist is finding out
items.summary: Sebnem Ece Eksi did a double take. Proteins typically studied in the brain were turning up in prostate cancer cells from high-risk patients. These proteins, called neuronal adhesion molecules, play a key role in the circuitry associated with memory. The finding, made during her Ph.D. days at the University of Illinois Chicago, raised so many questions to which Eksi is still seeking answers. Now at the Oregon Health & Science University in Portland, Eksi has made it her lab’s goal to find out how nervous systems communicate with cancer.

items.title: White Sands National Park: Things to Do & Where to Camp Nearby
items.summary: Picture this: you wax up a plastic saucer, push off the top of a sugar-white dune, and look up mid-run to see the jagged San Andres Mountains stretched across the horizon. Then you hike back up and do it again. And again, until the sun slips behind those peaks and the whole dunefield glows pink and gold. That’s what happens White Sands National Park, which protects much of the world’s largest gypsum dunefield: 275 square miles of glittering sand in southern New Mexico’s Tularosa Basin. The sand stays cool under bare feet even on warm days, the Sacramento Mountains light up at sunset, and once it’s dark, the stars put on a show of their own.

items.title: DOJ honors Goodyear police officer who rescued woman from burning car on I-10
items.summary: Officer Dakota Berry of Goodyear was recognized by the U.S. Department of Justice for his distinguished service.

items.summary: The staff for Shōzen, the television anime adaptation of Jiang Jia Meizi 's Chinese manhua Shang Shan, revealed a new trailer, key visual, and another cast member on Sunday. Kana Hanazawa plays Ko Kuka, Dōzen's childhood friend who shares a special bond with him. The series will debut on the B8station programming block on Fuji TV and other venues in April 2027. The story follows a Taoist priest Dōzen who encounters a young girl raised by supernatural creatures during his travels. He names the girl Shōzen, adopting her as his disciple, as he teaches her about human emotion and love.

items.title: curved concrete extension by belén ilarri studio updates 1970s house near valencia
items.summary: BELÉN ILARRI STUDIO REORGANIZES 1970S HOUSE IN VALENCIA Located on the outskirts of Valencia, Spain, Casa Lucerna is the renovation and extension of a 1970s residence by Belén Ilarri Studio. The intervention begins with the removal of a dropped hallway ceiling, uncovering the house’s concealed original ceiling height and structural proportions. Using this vertical recovery as its anchor, the studio reorganizes the floor plan around a cross-shaped circulation layout that links multiple orientations, frames sightlines toward the garden, and promotes cross-ventilation.

items.title: Commentary: Helping the Colorado River, one rock at a time

items.title: Mission: Yozakura Family Season 2 Anime's 2nd Part Casts Shinichirō Miki
items.summary: The staff for the anime of Hitsuji Gondaira 's Mission: Yozakura Family ( Yozakura-san Chi no Daisakusen ) manga announced on Sunday Shinichirō Miki will join the cast of the second part of the second season in episode 47, which airs on November 29. items.title: Forget 'Black Mirror,' These 10 Dark Sci-Fi Shows Take Dystopia Even Further
items.summary: The dystopian genre started taking shape around the early 20th century as a response to the political revolutions, widespread industrialization, and rising totalitarianism of the time, soon becoming one of the most prominent subgenres of science fiction. As such, it's no surprise that dystopian sci-fi has been one of television's most interesting genres for years, producing shows as fascinating as Black Mirror.

items.title: Indian opposition party’s youth wing warns of more Meta protests after police clashes
items.summary: Members of Congress party clashed with police outside tech company’s offices on Friday The youth wing of India’s main opposition Congress party warned of more protests against Meta’s removal of some of its members’ ⁠accounts, ⁠a day after clashing with ​police outside the tech firm’s locals offices. items.title: The Detective is Already Dead Anime's 2nd Season Reveals Trailer, Visual for New Arc

items.title: mono-material 3D printed children’s shoe expands five sizes and adapts to foot shape
items.summary: 3D PRINTED CHILDREN’S SHOE EXPANDS ACROSS FIVE SIZES Developed by footwear designer Daniel Winter, Fits is a 3D printed footwear system engineered to expand structurally as a foot grows or changes shape. Originating from a 2022 concept designed to prevent children from outgrowing shoes before their soles wear out, the refined children’s model expands across five full sizes and has completed wear testing. The structure operates through a mechanism termed ‘integral articulation’: a series of interconnected perimeter segments flex and roll outward as pressure is applied, widening the gaps between sections to increase volume while keeping the overall structure continuously joined.

items.title: Digital imaging workshop aims to reveal secrets in medieval manuscripts
items.summary: Researchers recently used multispectral imaging technology to try to uncover hidden information from medieval manuscripts at the Rare Book and Manuscript Library at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. The library hosted a digital imaging workshop in early October that served as a pilot study for how the technology can help analyze fragile, centuries-old documents.

items.title: The life, death and improbable rebirth of LA’s most beloved diner
items.summary: For decades, it served pancakes, hash browns and steaks to hungry Angelenos. Then came closure, and a city mourned – but now the Original Pantry is back Sometimes, an old-school American diner is just a diner. And sometimes, like the Original Pantry in downtown Los Angeles, it feels like the heart and soul of a city, a bellwether of good times and bad. For decades it was famous for never closing. Located in a low-slung shotgun building on a busy corner, it fed politicians, movie stars, students, criminals and street bums around the clock, seven days a week.

items.title: Europe is entering a ‘supercycle’ of national elections. Their outcomes could shake the EU’s foundations
items.summary: As nationalist, Eurosceptic parties surge in four of the bloc’s biggest member states, the coming year’s polls could test its resilience like never before In late 1998, Tony Blair was prime minister of Britain, Lionel Jospin was prime minister of France, and Gerhard Schröder had just been elected chancellor of Germany. The EU had 15 member states and pro-European, centre-left parties were in power – either alone or in coalitions – in all but two of them. Brisk economic growth was lifting living standards.

items.title: Libreboot Reverses AI Code Ban, Adopts Reduction Policy
items.summary: Libreboot, the free and open-source boot firmware project based on coreboot, has changed its approach to AI-generated code, replacing the complete ban from Libreboot 26.11 with a more flexible policy aimed at reducing AI involvement where practical. In a statement, project founder Lhehaa Rhoeow explained that the former prohibition was unrealistic, especially because Libreboot depends on upstream projects that already accept AI-assisted contributions. The new approach, called the “AI Slop Reduction Policy,” is intended to reduce AI-generated code through selective patch reversions, rewrites, and other measures without promising complete elimination.

items.title: KDE Plasma 6.9 to Improve Performance, NVIDIA Efficiency, and CJK Input
items.summary: KDE developers have shared another round of improvements planned for the upcoming Plasma 6.9 desktop environment, scheduled for release in late February. Starting with performance, KWin’s screenshot functionality has been optimized, allowing Spectacle and other applications using the compositor’s screenshot plugin to capture images faster. Another change adds overlay plane support for NVIDIA GPUs running driver version 615.78.08 or later, expected to reduce power consumption. KWin also gains better protection against problematic third-party plugins.

items.title: Following the “mathocalypse,” mathematicians consider the future

items.title: One Small Step
items.summary: How did Friday manage to leave a single footprint for Robinson Crusoe to discover? I went up the shore, and down the shore, but it was all one; I could see no other impression but that one. I went to it again to see if there were any more, and to observe if it might not be my fancy; but there was no room for that, for there was exactly the very print of a foot — toes, heel, and every part of a foot. How it came thither I knew not, nor could in the least imagine. “Was the single footprint made by some monstrous hopping cannibal?” asks John Sutherland in The Folio Book of Literary Puzzles (2007).

items.title: Drones strike Russian military-linked cargo ship in Gulf of Finland
items.summary: A Russian cargo ship linked to the country’s military logistics network caught fire after a drone attack in the Gulf of Finland on November 21, 2026. The damaged vessel drifted into Finnish territorial waters, where authorities coordinated a rescue and firefighting operation involving Finnish, Estonian and Russian units. The ship, Sparta II, was sailing from St. Petersburg toward Russia’s Kaliningrad exclave when it was hit. Finnish military officials said Ukraine was likely behind the attack, although Kyiv had not publicly claimed responsibility.

items.title: The Brutal Ways Emperor Valerian Executed Early Roman Popes
items.summary: For much of the Christian Church’s history, the Papacy has been an office sought by many members of the clergy. But in the 3rd century, accepting the “keys to the kingdom” meant almost certain death, with up to three-fourths of those who ascended to the papal throne dying in all sorts of horrendous ways at the hands of Roman authorities. While many emperors are responsible for ordering the deaths of popes, Emperor Valerian has the distinction of murdering more popes than any other. The Rising Prestige of the Christian Church From the time of its inception, the early Christian Church operated underground, hoping to escape the attention of the Roman authorities.

The approach reveals fine structures that brain wiring maps, known as connectomes, can miss.

items.title: 2 men killed after crash in north-central Phoenix Friday night
items.summary: PHOENIX (AZFamily) — Two people have died after a crash in north-central Phoenix Friday night. items.title: South Korea education minister resigns over exam cheating scandal
items.summary: South Korea's Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin has resigned over an exam cheating scandal that shocked the nation. items.title: Lock of former US President George Washington's hair sells for $4,000
items.summary: A framed lock of hair from America's first president, George Washington, has been sold at auction for $4,000 (Â£3,058). Saturday's sale is not the most expensive for Washington hair at auction. Three strands thought to have been removed from him close to or after his death stored in a locket sold for nearly $40,000 in 2021.

items.title: Why the An Lushan Rebellion Shattered the Tang Dynasty
items.summary: The Tang Dynasty (618 to 907 AD) enjoyed almost 300 years of supremacy in China. But one chaotic event pushed this prosperous dynasty to the brink of collapse, the An Lushan Rebellion. While the civil war lasted eight years, from 755 to 763 AD, its political and economic effects lasted decades, ultimately defining the long decline of the dynasty. The Fatal Flaw Hidden Behind China’s Golden Age Before the rebellion, the Tang Dynasty enjoyed a golden age under Emperor Xuanzong. However, its governance structure had weaknesses.

items.title: Sky Harbor officials tout vision, court contractors for massive terminal project
items.summary: With a new terminal set to be built at Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport, city and airport officials are starting to let designers and builders know what they expect in the project. items.title: The 15-Minute Battle of Quebec That Decided Who Would Rule North America
items.summary: On the morning of September 13, 1759, British and French troops faced each other on the Plains of Abraham outside Quebec City. The main fighting lasted barely fifteen minutes, yet it killed both commanders, James Wolfe and Louis-Joseph de Montcalm, and sealed the fate of French Canada. The clash was the climax of the Seven Years’ War in North America, the result of years of imperial rivalry and frontier warfare. Within four years, France had lost Canada, Britain controlled the continent east of the Mississippi, and the road to the American Revolution lay open.

items.title: Europe’s Modelled €5.70/kg Hydrogen Faces Industrial Buyers Who Can Afford Far Less
items.summary: Europe’s industrial hydrogen plans have a buyer problem. A factory cannot make its products competitive by paying whatever a new hydrogen plant needs to recover its investment. Its maximum hydrogen price is set by the cost of making the same product, or delivering the same useful heat, another way. The central 2050 scenario in my European hydrogen assessment puts on-site production at €5.70/kg. That starts with electricity at €60/MWh and 53 kWh of electricity per kilogram of hydrogen, so the electricity alone costs €3.18/kg.

items.title: China, ASEAN countries struggle over South China Sea code of conduct
items.summary: It was supposed to be a breakthrough year. The Philippines had intended to set up a code of conduct with China for the South China Sea during its 2026 ASEAN presidency. However, at the summit in Manila in mid-November they had to abandon their goal. Some 80% of the text had been negotiated, declared Philippine Foreign Secretary Theresa Lazaro, but the key areas of dispute had remained unsolved. Much more than diplomatic wording is at stake. The South China Sea is one of the world's most important shipping routes, it is rich in fishing grounds and may harbor significant oil and gas reserves.

items.title: 24 Airbus A380s Under Inspection Alert as Emirates, Etihad and Qantas Face Wing Crack Concerns
items.summary: TOULOUSE – Europe’s aviation regulator has expanded its inspection requirements for the Airbus A380 after concerns about cracks developing in the aircraft’s wing mid-spar structure. The European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) now requires 24 superjumbos to undergo inspections, increasing the number covered by its previous directive by eight aircraft. The updated Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2026-0216 took effect on November 18, 2026, replacing the emergency directive issued in June.

items.title: Alcohol may weaken cancer immunotherapy, early research suggests
items.summary: Cancer immunotherapy has transformed treatment for several advanced cancers, yet the difference between these treatments working and not could depend on simple routine habits. A recent study published in Science Signaling explores one such overlooked factor: regular alcohol consumption.

items.title: Time may be far stranger than we realize. Scientists have a way to test it
items.summary: Time may be far stranger than we realize, and scientists have proposed a way to detect clocks experiencing multiple flows of time simultaneously. Using atomic clocks with dramatically enhanced sensitivity, researchers hope to reveal a never-before-observed quantum effect that could transform our understanding of time and gravity.

items.title: Bayer reaches Roundup settlement that could cost the company billions
items.summary: The agrochemical and biotech giant Bayer has agreed to pay billions of dollars to people who sued the company alleging the weed-killer Roundup caused their cancer. On Friday, a judge in Missouri gave final approval to the nationwide settlement that could cost the company up to $7.25 billion in the coming years. The money will go to thousands of people who have been or will be diagnosed with non-Hodgkin lymphoma — a blood cancer that they claim is linked to glyphosate, which is the main ingredient in Roundup.

items.summary: Dashcam video captured the moment a missile struck a residential neighbourhood in Lviv, western Ukraine.

items.title: A giant star swallowed another star. James Webb reveals the aftermath
items.summary: Astronomers have witnessed a spectacular cosmic collision in the Andromeda galaxy, where a small star spiraled into a giant star 18,000 times brighter than the Sun, triggering a violent eruption. NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope captured the aftermath just 47 days later, revealing new details about how two stars can merge into one.

items.title: COP31 climate talks end without consensus on how to fund vulnerable countries or move the world away from coal, oil and gas use
items.summary: Almost two days into overtime, climate talks in the Turkish city of Antalya have collapsed as countries led by the European Union rejected a deal that critics say undermines the shift away from planet-heating fossil fuels. After two weeks of tough negotiations, the EU said it could not support the proposed agreement, known as the Antalya Pact, put forward by the COP presidency, saying it does not respond to the science. "We will not endorse a cover decision that does not even mention fossil fuels, the driver of climate change.

items.title: A 50-year-old theory about evolution may have been wrong all along
items.summary: A decades-old theory suggesting that evolution protects its most important genes from mutations has been dealt a major blow. An extensive new analysis of mutations in bacteria and yeast found no evidence that essential genes mutate less frequently than other genes. Researchers say earlier studies may have been misled by harmful mutations that disappeared through natural selection before scientists could detect them.

items.title: Despite soaring demand for GLP-1s, many eligible patients are unable to access these drugs for weight loss
items.summary: In just a few short years, glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists have surged in popularity across the United States, transforming from specialized treatments for type 2 diabetes into revolutionary therapeutics for weight management, cardiovascular health and other emerging uses. But not all populations are benefiting from this expansion. As GLP-1 use has increased, disparities in access to these drugs have widened significantly, according to a new study led by researchers at Boston University School of Public Health (BUSPH).

items.title: Italian jeweller and businessman Paolo Bulgari dies aged 89
items.summary: Italian jeweller Paolo Bulgari, who helped turn his family's business into a global luxury brand, has died in Rome aged age 89. His family announced the news, remembering him as "the greatest jeweller of our time", according to Italian media. Paolo Bulgari was Chairman of the Bvlgari Group since 1984 and its jewellery pieces have adorned Hollywood stars and royalty including Diana, Princess of Wales. The company Bvlgari posted an online tribute to the "true creative soul", whose work would "continue to inspire generations to come".

items.title: Elegance Flows Through Sheena Liam’s Embroideries in Green
items.summary: Model and ballet dancer Sheena Liam brings her understanding of poise, elegance, and graceful bodily movements to a more fixed medium. For the past several years, the artist has been stitching tender portraits of women with long, three-dimensional braids that cascade off the fabric. Occasionally, a single loose thread appears to have slipped out of its plait as it drifts across a protagonist’s cheek. Liam’s latest works are on view this month in her solo exhibition, The Unbearable Lightness. Several pieces feature figures sporting the same striped bodysuit with an open back, and the methodical pattern on the garment evokes both a sense of precision and rhythm depicted in the scenes.

items.title: Mexican drug lord on FBI's 10 most wanted list arrested in shoot-out
items.summary: A Mexican drug lord who was on the FBI's 10 most wanted list has been arrested following a shoot-out with Mexican authorities. Fausto Isidro "Chapo Isidro" Meza Flores and seven others were detained by Mexican special forces in Guasave, Sinaloa on Friday, Mexico's defence secretariat said. Seven suspects were killed in the operation, as were four members of the Mexican army who were travelling to reinforce security in Guasave, the secretariat added. Meza Flores was wanted in Mexico on organised crime charges, while he has been accused of "flooding the US with fentanyl, cocaine, heroin and other deadly drugs" by the FBI.

items.title: The European revolt may be coming to the UK
items.summary: The protests engulfing Europe represent a new level of popular mobilisation quite unlike any historical precedent. In France, Spain, Italy, Serbia, Germany and other countries across the continent, mass movements are challenging austerity and government failures. On Friday, the United Kingdom saw what is likely to be the beginning of its own wave of youth-driven demonstrations. Thousands of students walked out of hundreds of schools and universities around the country, from Aberdeen to Brighton, Swansea to Nottingham, making it one of the largest student mobilisations since the tripling of tuition fees back in 2010.

items.title: Why Somalia’s president turned against his former ally, the UAE
items.summary: Three years ago, at a town hall meeting in Mogadishu, Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud defended one of his country’s most controversial foreign partnerships. The United Arab Emirates, he declared, was “one of the greatest pillars” of Somalia’s war against the al-Qaeda-linked armed group al-Shabab. He praised Abu Dhabi’s support for the country’s armed forces despite longstanding concerns about its political influence. Having returned to power in 2022, Mohamud sought to repair relations with the Gulf state after a period of strained ties under his predecessor, while reassuring a sceptical Somali public that the UAE’s involvement was a boon rather than a hindrance.

items.title: 20 Years Ago Today: Hugh Jackman Starred In A Sci-Fi Movie That Divided Critics

items.title: Fragmented Landscapes
items.summary: I don’t think it’s a surprise at this point when I tell you that I love these artworks by Antwerp-based artist Joost Vandebrug. (I mean, tell me they don’t aesthetically rhyme with the KDO logo circles/moons…) Joost Vandebrug explores how separate views and moments come to be seen as a whole. His landscapes gather fragments into places that feel familiar, even when no single place could contain them. The image takes shape through remembering and looking, while the joins keep its construction visible.

items.title: When Your Winter Trip Has No Snow, Find Your Inner Daredevil Instead.
items.summary: I’ve never understood the appeal of roller coasters or similar thrill rides. The stomach-dropping plunges and screaming passengers who stumble off, then immediately get back in the perpetually long line? No, thank you. I’ve tried enough of them throughout my life to know they’re just not my thing. So imagine my surprise — or horror, or maybe a bit of both — when I found myself willingly, eagerly even, climbing into an Olympic bobsled, knowing I’d soon be barreling down an icy track at nearly 80 miles per hour, experiencing up to five times the force of gravity.

items.title: AOPA Aviation STEM Curriculum Reaches 160,000 Students
items.summary: The AOPA Foundation’s High School Aviation STEM Curriculum has reached more than 160,000 students since its introduction in 2017, according to a Nov. 19 update from the organization. The program currently serves approximately 34,000 students nationwide, providing high school courses focused on aviation and career pathways for pilots and drone operators. The curriculum is available at no cost to participating schools and includes seven courses across pilot and unmanned aircraft systems pathways. According to AOPA, more than 20% of students currently enrolled are female, while more than 60% of students who have completed the program report pursuing careers in aviation.

items.title: Will There Be a Season 2 of ‘Blade Runner 2099’?
items.summary: The future of the franchise. Prime Video's Blade Runner 2099 is an eight-episode limited series that expands the mythology of a science fiction universe that began with Philip K. Dick's 1968 novel Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep? The story first made its way to the big screen in Ridley Scott's 1982 classic Blade Runner, before continuing decades later with Blade Runner 2049 and the animated series Blade Runner: Black Lotus.

items.title: ‘Hellraiser: Revival’ Wins Horror Game of the Year; Doug Bradley Takes Best Performance!
items.summary: Clive Barker’s Hellraiser: Revival took home Game of the Year at tonight’s Horror Game Awards, beating a field that included Resident Evil Requiem. And even cooler, Doug Bradley earned Best Performance for returning as Pinhead! That is a huge win for this game and a franchise I’ve loved for decades. As much as I’ve championed Revival, seeing it take the top prize with a new Resident Evil in contention is still a stunning result. As we reported when nominations were announced, the original Game of the Year field included 16 titles.

items.title: Co-op bullet hell Temtem Swarm locks down a Nintendo Switch release date
items.summary: Say, are you a Nintendo Switch gamer who has looked on with bitter jealousy as Crema’s bullet hell co-op title Temtem Swarm has been played on other platforms? Well, fret not, little handheld and TV console owner because the game has officially confirmed its arrival to the Switch on Thursday, January 21st, 2027. Just in case…

items.title: Sovereignty starts with data, not chips, says Stuttgart AI factory chief
items.summary: A sovereign AI factory is only as valuable as the companies that can actually get onto it. Across Europe, publicly funded AI factories are racing to give startups and small manufacturers supercomputer-class GPUs without pushing them into lock-in or loose data handling. In Stuttgart, the HammerHAI AI factory is taking shape around a system from…

items.title: This Handmade Bluetooth Speaker Hides a Deadpan Face Behind its Grille
items.summary: Touch the body of the BLASÉ 01 and two narrow eyes slowly appear behind its fabric grille. They’re the sort of eyes that make you wonder if the speaker approves of your taste in music, though it doesn’t seem particularly invested either way. Hand-built in Vilnius, Lithuania, this Bluetooth loudspeaker is getting a first run of 20, each with that same sleepy stare. With its eyes dark, there’s something of a table lamp about it. A broad, matte olive head sits neatly on a tapered pedestal finished in oak veneer.

items.title: Microplastics may be more dangerous than we thought. Scientists just discovered why
items.summary: Microplastics may be doing something far more dangerous than simply accumulating in our bodies. Scientists have discovered that tiny plastic particles can interact with water to generate highly reactive molecules capable of damaging cells and tissues. This unexpected chemical activity could help explain growing evidence linking microplastic exposure to serious health problems, including heart attacks, strokes, and neurological disorders.

items.title: What Makes Notre-Dame Cathedral a Masterpiece of Gothic Architecture
items.summary: Most of us remember where we were when we heard that Notre-Dame had burned down. And even upon learning that the most famous of all French cathedrals had been badly damaged rather than completely destroyed, it still felt as if something irreplaceable had been lost. It made no difference whether we’d actually been to the place, as I hadn’t at the time. When I did finally make it to Paris four years later, Notre-Dame’s restoration was still underway, and construction walls prevented anyone from seeing much of anything at ground level, let alone entering.

items.title: ICE Arrests 2 Passengers Aboard Boarding Alaska Airlines Flight, Sparks Governor’s Fury
items.summary: SEATTLE – Federal immigration officers detained two passengers on the jet bridge at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (SEA) on Saturday, November 21, as travelers boarded an Alaska Airlines (AS) flight to Los Angeles International Airport (LAX). The arrests disrupted boarding and triggered criticism from Washington state officials, labor representatives, and airport authorities. The enforcement operation took place around 8 a.m. local time aboard Alaska Airlines Flight 1306, which was scheduled to depart for Los Angeles.

items.title: Army delays detonating "catastrophically hazardous" lead azide amid fear, anger
items.summary: In a swirl of questions, fears, and outrage, the US Army announced Thursday that it would delay a plan to blow up 68 deteriorating barrels of lead azide, which would launch toxic gas and lead into the air. A federal appeals court further halted plans later on Thursday with an emergency order. The plume, containing neurotoxic lead, could potentially drift 100 miles north of the Army installation housing it in Middletown, Iowa, according to modeling released by the Army earlier this week.

items.title: Preventable vision loss affects more than a billion people globally - and uneven access to care is the major culprit
items.summary: Around the world, more than 1 billion people are living with vision loss in their daily lives. For many, this means they don’t have the glasses they need to see clearly. For others, conditions such as cataracts, glaucoma, macular degeneration or diabetic eye disease have caused vision loss. The burden of this problem is not shared equally – 55% of those experiencing vision loss are women and girls, 73% are ages 50 and older, and 90% live in low- and middle-income countries. Age is the most important risk factor for vision loss.

items.title: Attorney general urges delay on 747-acre data center campus in Arizona
items.summary: Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes is hoping a vote on a proposed SpaceX data center project in Cochise County will be delayed.

items.title: ‘Barbie will be a grandmother’: Phoenix reacts to Mattel theme park plans
items.summary: From the stories making headlines to the restaurants, music and culture that make Phoenix one of a kind, New Times is there. Help us raise $25,000 by December 31 to keep independent local journalism going strong in 2027. Metro Phoenix’s reaction to VAI Resort’s plans for a bigger Mattel theme park in Glendale has more ups and downs than a roller coaster. On Monday, we reported that VAI Resort announced the long-delayed theme park has been renamed Mattel City and is growing to 14 acres. The multimillion-dollar project is also getting two new hotel towers, one housing the world’s first Barbie Hotel and another with a Mattel-inspired theme.

items.title: Inside Chandler's final push to build its own ambulance service as crews train for January launch
items.summary: At Chandler's Public Safety Training Center, the countdown is on. On January 14, seven ambulances with Chandler crews go into service. Four others will be on reserve. "This has been over two decades in the making that we have be wanting to make this a reality and it's imminent, it's here," said Avery Armstrong, battalion chief with the Chandler Fire Department. Chandler has hired outside companies to run its ambulances since 2002, five different companies. The city says that has meant high staff turnover and little control over where ambulances are stationed.

items.title: Here’s What The F130 Engines Will Change For B-52 Pilots During Aerial Refueling
items.summary: Footage from THE WATCH: America’s Nuclear Mission shows how demanding tanking is for B-52 crews, just as the B-52J’s new engines are about to change the way the bomber responds to the throttles. The B-52 episode of THE WATCH: America’s Nuclear Mission, the six-part documentary series created and produced by our friend and contributor Jeff Bolton of NFN Productions, follows a crew of the 5th Bomb Wing from Minot Air Force Base, North Dakota, callsign CHILL 42, through a full nuclear proficiency sortie, with additional footage filmed with the 2nd Bomb Wing at Barksdale Air Force Base, Louisiana.

items.title: Demo Arrives December 15 for Upcoming Psychological Horror Game ‘Perceptum’
items.summary: Taking the opportunity with being nominated for Most Anticipated Horror game, Perp Games and developer Duck Reaction have released a new trailer announcing a new demo for their upcoming psychological horror game, Perceptum. While the game is scheduled for release next year, you can grab the demo on December 15 on PC via Steam and the Epic Games Store. In Perceptum, you take on the role of a medium searching for a family that mysteriously vanished shortly after moving into their new home. Inside the house, familiar spaces feel wrong, silence becomes oppressive, and your senses cannot be trusted.

items.title: The Crucified Tongkonan of Tolu Deri in North Toraja Regency, Indonesia
items.summary: In the highland villages of North Toraja, the skyline is dominated by tongkonan —traditional ancestral houses with sweeping, boat-shaped saddle roofs that loom dramatically over the landscape. For centuries, these wooden structures have served as the spiritual and social anchor for Torajan clans, decorated strictly according to Aluk Todolo ("the way of the ancestors"), the indigenous animist belief system. Their facades are traditionally adorned with carved geometric patterns ( pa'ssura' ), water buffalo horns ( kabongo' ), and sculpted wooden heads ( katik ) symbolizing wealth, status, and protection.

items.title: ‘Longlegs’ Returns: Sterling K. Brown in Talks to Join Nicolas Cage in New Horror Entry
items.summary: Sterling K. Brown ( Paradise ) is in negotiations to join Paramount Pictures’ upcoming Longlegs film, reports Deadline. Brown would be joining Nicolas Cage, who will be reprising his iconic role as the titular character. Osgood Perkins is back to direct and is also writing and producing. The update follows our recent report that Maika Monroe won’t return as FBI agent Lee Harker. Speaking with ScreenRant while promoting Victorian Psycho, she said, “Lee Harker will not be in this one,” although she “would love to revisit that role.”

items.title: BADBOX botnet returns with record-breaking 40 billion daily ad requests
items.summary: The BADBOX malware found in a broad range of generic Android TV boxes has returned to large-scale ad-fraud operations following last year's disruptions.

items.title: Tiny egg-eating snake discovered in Ethiopia
items.summary: Biologists have discovered multiple new species of egg-eating snakes slithering through the forests near southeastern Ethiopia’s Bale Mountains. Although researchers only described the white-throated egg-eater ( Dasypeltis albigularis ) in their study recently published in the journal Herpetozoa, they promised that information on additional finds is on the way. “Three other species in this genus are still waiting in line,” Arthur Tiutenko, a study co-author and herpetologist at Germany’s Friedrich-Alexander University of Erlangen–Nuremberg (FAU), said in a statement.

items.title: Invincible Gets a Season 5 Release Date, Pokes Fun at its Least Popular Episode
items.summary: Yesterday, Prime Video released a teaser for Invincible season 5 confirming that Mark Grayson is returning earlier than expected (February 17, to be precise.) By now, most fans know what to expect from these teasers: Mark will sit in Burger Mart, usually holding a conversation about the events of the previous season with another character. This time, it’s demonic detective Damian Darkblood (Clancy Brown). Unlike the other Burger Mart teasers, however, this moment features Mark going off on Darkblood.

items.title: I Walked Solo Along England’s Rugged South West Coast Path for Three Days
items.summary: I’m standing atop a spit of land jutting out into the English Channel, peering down at a beach accessible only by boat, where a small group of sunbathers lounge on the rocky sand. The view is a welcome excuse to catch my breath before continuing along five more rolling cliffs—400 steep feet up, 400 steep feet down, and repeat. And so, despite my exhausted legs and the blister that’s forming over my right big toe, I decide to imprint this impossibly peaceful scene into my brain to remind myself why I’m doing this trip.

items.title: Google rolls out new search homepage with AI chat history and no search button
items.summary: Google's flagship search experience is evolving into an AI experience with stunning speed. Even time-tested elements of search are getting AI makeovers, and the latest to get this treatment is the search homepage on Google.com. A redesign that's been in testing for the last few weeks is now official, bringing easier access to AI chats and dropping the dedicated search button entirely. Google search VP Robby Stein confirmed on X that Google is deploying the new desktop search page after a successful test.

items.title: Meta reconsiders 2030 net-zero goal amid record emissions from AI data centers
items.summary: Meta’s executives are rethinking the company’s original goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2030. That revelation in Meta’s latest sustainability report comes as the company reported a record percentage increase in greenhouse gas emissions that exceeds any other Big Tech competitor racing to build new AI data centers. The company’s 2026 sustainability report claims that “our long-term ambitions haven’t changed, but our operating environment has,” according to an introduction from Rachel Peterson, vice president of data centers at Meta, and Blair Swedeen, global head of net zero and sustainability at Meta.

Before a banker can recommend an acquisition to their client, they need to make sense of financial statements, customer contracts and management presentations.

items.title: ‘Echograph’ Preview: ‘Fatal Frame’-Inspired Low-Poly Game Nails Classic Survival Horror
items.summary: As more and more mainstream, big budget horror games seem to shift towards an action-focused mindset, we’ve seen the indie space pick up the mantle of classic survival horror. While many of them draw their inspiration from titans of the genre like Silent Hill or Resident Evil, we rarely see games that try to mimic the iconic Fatal Frame series. With the Fatal Frame II Remake having come out earlier this year, it seems like we’re poised to have a renaissance for that style, and games like Echograph, the debut game from Pappy’s Pipe Dream, look to lead the charge.

items.title: Quoting Levent Alpöge
items.summary: I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis. In fact, the method easily extends much further, resolving the so-called Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, and I expect, with more time, the Extended Riemann Hypothesis too. Claude and I have also formalized the arguments without assumptions. It is natural to feel that this is an end, in my case a loss of a principal guiding light, but what I saw during the course of progress so amazed me that I believe it is one dawn across science of something far greater.

items.title: Researcher plants 2m canaries into the AI supply chain. A privacy disaster surfaced.
items.summary: Researchers planted 2 million digital tripwires in requests sent through a sprawling network of AI services to find out what happened to sensitive information entrusted to them. What they discovered was an ecosystem that leaked highly sensitive data like a sieve. The exposure was found through an ingenious experiment designed to test if sensitive information can leak through the vast chain of widely used AI services and how that information is exploited when it does. Many of today’s AI apps use services such as OpenRouter or Vercel that act as brokers.

items.title: Anthropic says it will put humanity first. Will its IPO change that?
items.summary: As Anthropic executives and co-founders gathered to celebrate the artificial intelligence company's market debut at the Nasdaq stock exchange on Thursday, CEO Dario Amodei spoke about AI's potential benefits, and risks, to humanity. "There is a gigantic difference between how AI will go if we pay little attention to safety versus how it will go if we are obsessed with safety," Amodei said before ringing the ceremonial opening bell. "And an obsession with safety and public benefit has been built into Anthropic's DNA from the start."

items.title: JetBrains Air in GoLand: Build, Review, and Profile Go Code With Agents
items.summary: If you’ve ever built backend services in Go, chances are you’ve also written a webhook handler or two. They’re small and rarely get much attention – that is, until something breaks. A third-party provider sends a signed request, and then you check the signature, store the event, and reply. Sounds like three easy steps, but a lot can go wrong. A captured request could get replayed, a duplicate could get saved twice, or a forged signature could slip through. Coding agents are not likely to make these types of mistakes, so with code becoming cheaper to generate, handlers are a good task to give them.

items.title: 7 Old-Fashioned Words That Describe Beauty
items.summary: Society has always had, and will always have, shifting standards of beauty. Each year, decade, and century, across oceans and cultures, we're given new ideals to marvel at and obsess over, from facial features to style to settings. While this seems unavoidable, especially in the digital era, true beauty remains in the eye of the beholder. Beauty, by definition, is âthe quality or group of qualities in a person or thing that gives pleasure to the senses or the mind.â And since we all have different minds, a physical âbeauty standardâ is a very loose concept with a very strong hold on society.

items.title: The AI boom had a really bad week — and it's raising loud alarms
items.summary: A yearslong AI boom showed signs of unraveling this week in spectacular fashion. AI-related stocks have powered markets to record highs and helped support the broader economy. But investors now fear that a potential bubble in the sector could be bursting, which could spark wider financial repercussions. Investors were hoping the stock market debut of AI giant Anthropic this week would provide a boost to the markets. Instead, the entire stock market got pummeled on Friday, sparking one of the worst weeks that Wall Street has seen in quite some time.

items.title: Aspen Approves 60% Increase in GA Landing Fees
items.summary: Pitkin County commissioners have approved a 60% increase in general aviation landing fees at Aspen/Pitkin County Airport (ASE) for 2027. According to a county announcement Thursday, the new rates will rise from $13.76 to $22.04 per 1,000 pounds of aircraft weight as the airport prepares for a seven-month closure for runway reconstruction. Commissioners Reduce Proposed Increase The approved rates are lower than earlier proposals that would have raised GA landing fees by approximately 140%. County officials said airlines and general aviation operators had raised concerns about the proposed increases, prompting airport staff to develop a revised funding plan.

items.title: F-35A Demo Team Moves Back To Luke AFB
items.summary: After moving to Hill AFB in 2019, the U.S. Air Force’s F-35A Lightning II Demo Team is now returning to Luke AFB, where it was originally created in 2016. The U.S. Air Force’s F-35A Lightning II Demonstration Team announced on Nov. 20, 2026, that it is preparing to return to Luke Air Force Base, Arizona. The team was initially created at Luke AFB in 2016 as F-35 Heritage Flight Team, before it was moved to Hill AFB, Utah, in 2019. The move to Hill AFB coincided with the transition of the team under Air Combat Command with the 388th Fighter Wing.

items.title: 7 European Villages That Look Even More Magical in the Snow
items.summary: And while many of us plan entire trips around this weather, a handful of alpine destinations across Europe make us question just how important the warmth really is when the alternative is a stunning, snow-covered scene that looks handpicked from the coziest film you've ever seen. Here are seven European villages that are fun to explore year-round, but look even more magical in the snow. The Jungfrau Ski Region officially opens for the season on November 29, offering miles upon miles of runs and winter fun for skiers of all ages.
